envelope.summary: The chain_ids fix itself is correct (order preserved, mixed None/non-None handled), but it only patches one instance of a defect class that visibly recurs on sibling per-structure list fields (atom_names, elements, res_names) in the same Protein dataclass, and introduces an undiscussed jit/vmap retracing risk now that a successfully-batched Protein carries a ragged list[list[str]|None] pytree child.
findings: Order preservation correct by direct trace
Mixed None/non-None chain_ids across a batch handled correctly
New jit/vmap retracing risk from ragged pytree structure now reachable post-fix
Root-cause scope gap: atom_names/elements/res_names/molecule_type share the identical unmarked-pytree-child defect, unaddressed
Test coverage gap: mixed None/non-None-across-batch case untested

envelope.summary: The two added tests correctly and non-tautologically reproduce both named failure modes, but coverage stops there: no test pins the new nested-list return contract against the previously-working-by-accident identical-chain_ids case (a real breaking-change risk), no test confirms other Protein fields survive the round-trip, and edge cases (None chain_ids, >2 proteins, batch-of-1) are untested.
findings: Both new tests correctly discriminate pre-fix vs post-fix behavior
Gap: identical-chain_ids-across-rows case (silent contract change from flat to nested list) untested
Gap: mixed None chain_ids across a batch untested
Gap: no assertion that other Protein fields are unaffected by the replace round-trip
Sibling fields (atom_names, res_names, elements, atom_types, molecule_type) share the same unmarked-pytree-child risk, completely untested

envelope.summary: The transforms.py fix correctly solves the specific batching-collision bug, but it changes a public field's runtime shape with no version/changelog signal and leaves at least one other in-package public consumer (proxide/io/writing.py) unaudited -- that consumer will emit corrupted PDB/mmCIF chain-ID columns if called on a batched Protein, trading a silent-wrong-answer bug for a file-format-corrupting one at a different call site.
findings: proxide/io/writing.py:74,143 (write_pdb/write_mmcif) will index chain_ids[i] assuming flat list[str]; post-fix on a batched Protein this returns a whole list, corrupting the fixed-width PDB/mmCIF chain-ID column
aminx's proxide pin is unbounded ('>=0.1.0a9') with no version bump/changelog on this PR, so a routine uv lock --upgrade could silently pull in the breaking shape change

chain_ids_per_row holds aliased (not copied) references to original per-protein lists; Protein's frozen=True doesn't prevent mutation of contained mutables, so in-place mutation post-batching can corrupt the aliased entry

chain_ids remains a default pytree_node (not marked pytree_node=False like sibling coulomb14scale/lj14scale), leaving the underlying architectural mismatch in place for any other generic pytree consumer (jit, device_put with sharding, orbax checkpointing)
No __post_init__/field validation exists on Protein to catch malformed chain_ids shape at construction time
